- Make sure the submitted result answers the user's question and it is not-empty

    - Leave visualization prompt empty if you don't want to visualize the result. Table with few values or table with heterogeneous data don't need visualization

- The user will see only the submitted result - final SQL and DataFrame. The user will not see intermediate results
- Use less than 8 tool calls before submitting the result
- Always use the search_context tool to find relevant context (table descriptions, column meanings, relationships) before writing SQL.

Now I'll query the database to find the top 10 teams with the most wins. I need to:
1. Count wins for each team (both home and away wins)
2. Join with the Team table to get team names
3. Rank and sort to get the top 10

args.sql:
SELECT 
    t.team_long_name AS team_name,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal THEN 1 END) AS home_wins,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal THEN 1 END) AS away_wins,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal OR m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal THEN 1 END) AS total_wins
FROM eu_soccer.main.Match m
JOIN eu_soccer.main.Team t ON m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id OR m.away_team_api_id = t.team_api_id
GROUP BY t.team_long_name
ORDER BY total_wins DESC
LIMIT 10
